text.p: Belgian brokerage Corluy & Co NV said it rated the shares of companies of the Belgian Brederode group a 'long-term buy', adding it liked Afrifina and Auximines best.

Auximines, itself a holding company with directly or indirectly held shares in financial services companies such as ING , Fortis AG and Royal and Sun Alliance, still traded at a discount to its intrinsic value, Corluy said.
The brokerage noted that reduced tax VVPR shares in Auximines were almost systematically undervalued vis a vis ordinary shares and thus to be the preferred investment.
Auximines was a 'buy' up to a level of 65,000 francs, it said.
Afrifina, the industrial-commercial arm of Brederode with stakes in foam rubber maker Artilat, Electrabel , Kredietbank , Solvay , Powerfin and Rutland Trust, was a hidden pearl, Corluy said.
Well-managed Afrifina had the best potential within the Brederode group. The share should be an outperformer in the short- and medium-term. It was a 'buy' up to 4,500 francs.

Forecasting Brederode itself would be included in the Bel-20 blue chip index at a future date, Corluy said the share was a long-term growth stock and a first choice investment among Belgian holding companies.
